messages:
Sam (Billing): Heads up 10 Lyra Therapeutics invoice 14901 shows a promotional credit applied to a paid invoice and then a refund processed twice. Need to clean up and issue a single correct credit or refund.
Devon (Account Exec): Customer flagged via support: they were refunded $3,600 twice for a promo that should have been a one-time $3,600 credit. They only requested one refund.
Sam (Billing): Pulled lines: ```
Invoice: 14901
Customer: Lyra Therapeutics (US, MA)
Period: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30
Charges: Usage & Dedicated: $18,000.00
Promo LYRA-ONE-TIME: -$3,600.00
Refund processed: -$3,600.00 (processed 2026-12-02)
Refund processed: -$3,600.00 (processed 2026-12-03 duplicate)
Total: $7,200.00 (system shows negative ledger earlier)
```
Sam (Billing): Looks like webhook retry caused the second refund job to run; refund job id rj-778 and rj-779. Billing ledger shows negative cash until we net one refund back.
Priya (Head of Billing): We need to: 1) determine whether to reverse duplicate refund (i.e., charge customer back) or 2) treat as accounting correction and issue internal journal to treasury to recover funds. Customer prefers not to be charged again; they want us to fix on our side.
Devon (Account Exec): Agreed. They asked us to absorb the duplicate refund and not debit them. Can we reclassify second refund as treasury recovery and tag to misc-expense instead of taking money back from customer?
Sam (Billing): billing-bot, show refund transactions and create reversal entry proposal.
billing-bot: Refunds found: RJ-778 amount 3600 USD (status: COMPLETED) txn_id=pay_xxx_aa. RJ-779 amount 3600 USD (status: COMPLETED) txn_id=pay_xxx_bb. Duplicate detected by matcher with similarity 0.98. Proposed action: create CM-2026-1402 reversing one refund OR create journal JE-2026-1402 to reclassify RJ-779 cash movement to misc-expense after coordination with Treasury.
Priya (Head of Billing): Tax check first. tax-bot, any tax consequences for reversing a refund or reclassifying as expense for MA customer?
tax-bot: Refund reversal increases revenue post-period; reclassification to misc-expense does not change original taxable event. For MA, SaaS typically non-taxable for this customer. No additional sales tax effects. However, revenue recognition must be adjusted. Recommend using journal + treasury recovery instead of rebilling the customer.
Priya (Head of Billing): Ok approve internal recovery route. We will not charge the customer back. Sam  coordinate with Treasury and create journal. Also add internal memo stating customer consent obtained.
Sam (Billing): Uploaded support thread: lyra_support_20261204.eml and refund_audit_rj-778_779.pdf. billing-bot, create journal JE-2026-1402 reclassify RJ-779 to misc-expense and create memo CM-2026-1402 tagging lyra-duplicate-refund for audit.
billing-bot: JE-2026-1402 created (DRAFT) reclassify cash 3600 USD -> misc_expense. CM-2026-1402 created (DRAFT) amount 3600 USD reason="duplicate refund reclassification; customer to be spared debit". Attachments: refund_audit_rj-778_779.pdf, lyra_support_20261204.eml.
Priya (Head of Billing): Approve JE and CM. Approve up to $10k for internal recovery reclassifications without exec. Add memo: "Customer requested we not charge them back; treasury to treat as misc-expense and pursue internal cost recovery from operations team if needed."
Sam (Billing): billing-bot, move CM-2026-1402 to APPROVED and post JE-2026-1402.
billing-bot: CM-2026-1402 moved to APPROVED and JE-2026-1402 posted. Cash reclassification executed; AR unchanged. Journal posted JE-2026-1402. Treasury notified to reconcile pay_xxx_bb. RevOps flagged revenue impact for December close.
Devon (Account Exec): Customer replied: "Thank you for handling this without charging us back  much appreciated." :relieved:
Sam (Billing): Closing thread. Filing CM and JE paperwork to December month-end bundle. Creating engineering ticket MG-2509 to prevent duplicate refund processing on webhook retries.
